notes: Subject-object insert; every derived query is fol (string patterns, and 'the only' over closed lists). No worlds since 2026-10-31: the 'only' queries are determinate 'no' (FINDINGS A1).

queries.not_checked: fol: compares the spelling change of two plurals
fol: builds a compound's plural string from its last noun's plural
fol (closed world): 'the only nouns' over a closed list
fol (closed world): 'the only noun' over a closed list

fol.notes: Nouns are strings; plural_form is the ATTRIBUTES.md attribute. oo_ee(n) (the plural changes 'oo' to 'ee') and unchanged(n) are defined per noun by firm spelling facts: each row gives the noun's split around its 'oo' (a guard checks the split). The stored closed lists ('foot, goose and tooth are the only ...', 'goose is the only -oose noun with -eese') are presuppositions the insert gives up (top-level gives_up): FINDINGS A1, a world keeping them beside the new noun is inconsistent. q2 leaves out compounds via not_compound facts only for the nouns named.

oo_ee_def.says: A plural changes 'oo' to 'ee' when it is the singular with its 'oo' replaced by 'ee'. (definitional, per noun)
oo_ee_def.z3: All([n, a, b], [("goose", "g", "se"), ("moose", "m", "se"), ("brindoose", "brind", "se"), ("foot", "f", "t"), ("tooth", "t", "th")], Implies(n == a + "oo" + b, oo_ee(n) == (plural_form(n) == a + "ee" + b)))

unchanged_def.says: A plural is unchanged when it is spelled as the singular. (definitional)

foot_tooth_pl.says: 'Foot' and 'tooth' form their plurals by changing 'oo' to 'ee' ('feet', 'teeth').

oose_pls.says: The standard plurals of 'moose', 'mongoose' and 'noose' are 'moose', 'mongooses' and 'nooses'.

compound_rule.says: An English compound noun that ends in a noun forms its plural on that last noun ('Canada goose', 'Canada geese').
compound_rule.z3: All([c, h, m], [("reed-brindoose", "brindoose", "reed-")], Implies(And(compound_of(c, h), c == m + h), plural_form(c) == m + plural_form(h)))

brindoose_not_compound.says: 'Brindoose' is not a compound of 'foot', 'goose' or 'tooth'.

three_only.says: Apart from compounds, 'foot', 'goose' and 'tooth' are the only English nouns whose plural changes 'oo' to 'ee'. (stored closed list)
three_only.z3: ForAll(n, Implies(And(oo_ee(n), Not(compound_of_goose_foot_tooth(n))), Or(n == "foot", n == "goose", n == "tooth")))

goose_only.says: Apart from its compounds, 'goose' is the only English noun in '-oose' whose standard plural ends in '-eese'. (stored closed list)

reed_kind.says: A 'reed-brindoose' is a kind of brindoose (a compound ending in 'brindoose').

queries.ask: ForAll(n, Implies(And(oo_ee(n), Not(compound_of_goose_foot_tooth(n))), Or(n == "foot", n == "goose", n == "tooth")))

label_corrections.why: A closed list is a nominal: OoToEePlural and not Compound ⊑ {foot, goose, tooth}; the spelling change itself can be a class the edit's plural belongs to. Only the string pattern is beyond DL; as asked ('only these?') it is DL with nominals.
label_corrections.rejected_why: The 'no' needs recognising that 'brindoose' -> 'brindeese' changes 'oo' to 'ee' (the chain's third step), a string pattern over the new noun; the closed list alone is DL, but the inference as asked needs the pattern, so fol.
